title: What does the XRPL AllowTrustLineClawback account flag mean?
abstract: Sourced explanation of AllowTrustLineClawback and its practical limits.
body:
According to XRPL documentation, AllowTrustLineClawback irreversibly gives an issuer the ability to claw back its own trust-line tokens. [1]

The AccountSet reference requires an empty owner directory before activation. An issuer therefore needs to decide before creating trust lines and other owned objects. It cannot later disable this setting, and NoFreeze has an incompatible relationship. Holders should inspect the issuer's actual ledger settings rather than infer token rights from the currency symbol. [1][2]

XRPL distinguishes an AccountSet option from the AccountRoot bit that records the resulting state. SetFlag and ClearFlag use option identifiers, while the ledger Flags field stores bit values; the numbers are not interchangeable. Read the documented mapping for AllowTrustLineClawback and check the validated account state after any permitted change. A successful submission response alone does not establish that the requested state is final. [1][2]

Author interpretation: document why AllowTrustLineClawback is needed, who may authorize a change and what existing users would experience. Review irreversible settings before issuance and test reversible settings with representative counterparties. This is guidance for interpreting account controls, not a live network measurement. Sources accessed 10 November 2026.
